description: The plot illustrates the search space size of the M-Cube dataset under different configurations, measured as the number of possible solutions as a function of the number of missing pieces. The x-axis, labeled "# Missing pieces," ranges from 1 to 6 on a linear scale, representing the number of pieces that are absent from the cube. The y-axis, labeled "# Possible solutions," is on a logarithmic scale, spanning from $10^2$ to $10^8$, indicating the vast range of potential configurations. Three distinct configurations are compared: "Flip needed" (orange line with circular markers), "Flip ignored" (blue line with circular markers), and "CUBE-easy" (red text label). The "Flip needed" configuration shows the largest search space, starting at approximately $10^4$ solutions for one missing piece and increasing to over $10^8$ for six missing pieces. The "Flip ignored" configuration has a smaller search space, starting at about $10^2$ solutions and rising to approximately $10^6$ for six missing pieces. The "CUBE-easy" configuration is represented by a red label at the point corresponding to six missing pieces and a search space of over $10^8$ solutions, suggesting it is a specific case or subset of the "Flip needed" scenario.
